chunks: Determining motor position. The question: How can you determine the position of a motor?
To know where a motor shaft is pointing, pick a sensor that fits the job. An absolute sensor tells you the angle the moment it powers up.
An incremental sensor only counts movement, so it needs a starting reference.
Some motors need no extra sensor: a stepper counts its steps, and a brushless motor's Hall sensors give a rough angle.
Always ask about resolution, absolute versus relative, environment, and cost.
Think of a hotel hallway. Absolute sensing is like door numbers: step out of the elevator and you instantly know where you are.
Incremental sensing is like counting your steps from the elevator.
It can be very precise, but if you lose count, or leave the building and return, you must walk back to the elevator to start over. That return trip is homing.
A first-pass selection tree. Most small actuators end up in "magnetic angle sensor" (absolute) or "incremental encoder with a homing switch".
Absolute sensor: reports a unique angle at power-up, such as a potentiometer (a variable resistor), magnetic angle sensor, or absolute encoder.
Incremental encoder: outputs pulses as the shaft turns, so the controller keeps a running count.
Homing: moving to a known reference, such as a limit switch or index pulse, to set zero.
Resolution vs accuracy: the smallest step the sensor reports, versus how close it is to the true angle.
A 12-bit absolute magnetic sensor splits one turn into 2 to the 12 equals 4096 positions, so each is 360 over 4096 equals 0. 088° .
Incremental: a 12-line encoder gives 4 countable edges per line, so 48 counts per motor turn. Through a 30:1 gearbox that is 48 times 30 equals 1440 counts per output turn, 0.
25° each. A brushless motor's three Hall (magnetic) sensors give 6 readings per magnetic cycle.
With 7 pole pairs (north-south magnet pairs), that is 42 readings per turn, so it knows its position only to about 8. 6°. That is the whole idea.
"I'd pick between absolute and incremental. Absolute options are a potentiometer, a magnetic angle sensor (12 bits or more, contactless) or an absolute encoder.
Incremental means an optical quadrature encoder, which needs homing at power-up. Brushless motors have Hall sensors good for commutation (about 60 electrical degrees).
Steppers count steps if they don't slip. The gear ratio multiplies output resolution but adds backlash. I'd choose on resolution, absolute versus relative, environment and cost."
